text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Austria's defence ministry plans to buy more than 500 tanks, an order worth five billion schillings.
- The coming two years will be difficult for Austria's telecoms monopoly ahead of its planned privatisation in 1999, finance chief Johannes Ditz said.
- Health Minister Christa Krammer insists genetically manipulated foodstuffs should be labeled properly.

- Austrian industrialists welcome Italian lira's return into the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) but warn the currency will have to prove its stability ahead of Europe's planned monetary union.
- Siemens Nixdorf Informationssysteme (SNI), a unit of Germany's Siemens group, posted a record turnover of 3.2 billion schillings in the year to September 30, up from 3.1 billion the year before.
- Austria's Finance Ministry confirmed it received two indicative bids for the government's 70 percent voting stake in bank Creditanstalt.
DIE PRESSE
- The lira's return into the ERM will benefit Austrian exporters and the country's tourism industry, Finance Minister Viktor Klima says.
- A record 30 billion schillings will be invested by foreign companies in Austria this year, research institute Wifo says.
- Sources say Bank Austria and Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank (WestLB) may team up to bid for Creditanstalt, rivalling the only known bid for the bank by a group around insurer EA-Generali.
- Hospital staff threaten to go on strike unless an agreement on working hours can be found this week.
- House prices poised to rise over the next few months as investors put more money into real estate ahead of Europe's planned single currency, real estate brokers say.
- Austrian exports to South Africa reached almost two billion schillings last year, while imports from the country stood at about 1.1 billion, trade officials say.
KURIER
- New telephone tariff structure should lead to lower overall phone costs, while costs for some local calls may increase from 1998, telecoms monopoly says.
- Austria's federal trade union congress plans a complete overhaul of its structures.
- An Austrian who was on board an Ethiopian airliner that was hijacked and then crashed near the Comores islands off the African coast is presumed dead.
- OPEC ministerial meeting kicks off in Vienna on Wednesday.
- Austria's electricity industry wants to put up barriers against cheap electricity imports from eastern Europe, citing environmental concerns.
- Demand for shares of motorbike maker KTM is buoyant.
- The number of banks licensed to take part in Austrian government bond tenders will be raised to 17 from 11 currently by next year.
- GE Capital named as possible bidder for Creditanstalt.
